config.title: Event Handling

intro.title: Event Handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button component that changes its appearance when clicked. You will learn the core concept of event handling in React, which allows your application to respond to user actions like clicks. The main technologies involved are React's onClick event handler and TypeScript for type-safe function definitions. By the end, you'll understand how to capture events and update the UI dynamically in a React TypeScript application.
intro.usecase: Event handling is fundamental to every interactive web application. In real-world React applications, you'll use event handlers for form submissions in login screens, button clicks in e-commerce checkout flows, and input changes in search filters. Developers implement event handling when building interactive dashboards with real-time data updates, modal windows with close buttons, and navigation menus with hover effects. Mastering event handling allows you to create responsive UIs that react to user actions in applications like project management tools, social media platforms, and financial analytics dashboards.

objectives: Apply event handler functions to respond to user interactions in React components.
Implement TypeScript type annotations for event parameters to ensure type safety.
Use the onClick prop to handle click events on button elements.
Define inline arrow functions to pass event handlers directly to JSX elements.
Construct controlled input components by handling onChange events.
Utilize event objects to access target values from form inputs.
Assign state variables to store and update data based on user events.
Invoke setState functions within event handlers to trigger UI updates.
Handle form submission events to prevent default browser behavior.
Control component behavior by passing event handlers as props to child components.
Modify component state based on multiple event types within a single component.
Return appropriate JSX structures that include event handlers for interactive elements.

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement at the top of your file to import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by curly braces containing the names you want to import, then specify the package name in quotes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement must include both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. The component should be defined with TypeScript and return a JSX element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to include the return type annotation : JSX.Element for TypeScript.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: The code defines a component named App (either as a function or arrow function) with a return statement that returns JSX. The component includes the TypeScript return type annotation : JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component returns JSX and includes the : JSX.Element type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a component named App that returns JSX with the proper TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Initialize count state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a state variable named 'count' using useState, initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the initial value (0) and destructure the returned array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a number state
const [count, setCount] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a count state variable initialized to 0, ready to be displayed and updated later.
successCriteria: The code must include a useState call with initial value 0, destructured into a variable named 'count' and its setter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the count state with useState. The count variable now holds the value 0, and setCount can be used to update it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0 and destructuring it into a variable named 'count'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to declare a state variable called 'count' using useState, initialized to 0.

steps.title: Define handleIncrement function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleIncrement that increments the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with the current count plus 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleIncrement function is defined and can be called to update the count state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleIncrement function that will update the count state when called.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named handleIncrement and it calls setCount to increment the current count by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleIncrement function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function with the right name that updates the count state.

steps.title: Define handleDecrement function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleDecrement that decreases the count state by 1 when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with the current count minus 1. You can use the previous state to calculate the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleDecrement function that properly updates the count state.
successCriteria: The function must be named handleDecrement, call setCount, and decrease the count value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleDecrement function that decreases the count state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleDecrement function properly calls setCount to decrease the count by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDecrement function isn't defined correctly. It should call setCount to decrease the count state by 1.

steps.title: Define handleReset function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named handleReset that resets the count state to 0. The function should have no parameters and return void.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with the value 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReset function that resets the count state to 0 when called.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleReset function that will reset the count to 0.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your handleReset function calls setCount(0) to reset the count state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleReset function isn't quite right. It should be a function that calls setCount(0) to reset the count state to 0.

steps.title: Return a container div
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, replace the existing div with a new div that will serve as the main container for your event handling UI.
steps.hint: The return statement should have a single top-level div element. This div will wrap all the content you'll add later.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a div element that will contain the event handling UI.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element
The div is the top-level JSX element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the container div that will hold all your event handling UI elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the return statement has a div element as its top-level JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should contain a div element to serve as the main container for your UI.

steps.title: Add a heading displaying the count
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, add an <h2> element that displays the current count value. Place it after the existing <h1> element.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to embed the count variable in the heading text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a heading that displays the current count value, which is initially 0.
successCriteria: An <h2> element is added after the existing <h1>
The <h2> element contains the count variable inside curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a heading that displays the current count value. This demonstrates how to embed state variables directly in JSX.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added an <h2> element that displays the count variable using curly braces like {count}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading displaying the count wasn't added correctly. Remember to add an <h2> element after the existing <h1> and use curly braces to embed the count variable.

steps.title: Add increment button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and wire its onClick event to the handleIncrement function.
steps.hint: Use the onClick prop on a <button> element and pass handleIncrement as the handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleIncrement}>Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Increment' appears in the UI, and clicking it will increase the count by 1.
successCriteria: The button element must have the text 'Increment' and its onClick prop must be set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that triggers the increment function when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Increment' and its onClick is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or incorrectly configured. Check that you've added a <button> with onClick={handleIncrement} and the text 'Increment'.

steps.title: Add decrement button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button with the text 'Decrement' and wire its onClick event to the handleDecrement function.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the container div, set its text to 'Decrement', and use onClick={handleDecrement} to connect it to the handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleDecrement}>Decrement</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Decrement' button appears below the count display, and clicking it will call the handleDecrement function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Decrement button and connected it to the handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check if the text is 'Decrement' and the onClick is correctly set to handleDecrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly wired. Ensure you add a <button> with text 'Decrement' and onClick={handleDecrement}.

steps.title: Add reset button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Reset' and wire its onClick event to the handleReset function.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the return statement, set its text content to 'Reset', and pass handleReset to the onClick prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleReset}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Reset' button appears in the UI that, when clicked, will call the handleReset function (to be defined in the next step).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the Reset button and wired it to the handleReset function. The button is now ready to trigger the reset functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a button with the exact text 'Reset' and that its onClick prop is set to handleReset.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Reset button isn't properly configured. Check that you've added a button element with text 'Reset' and wired its onClick to handleReset.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be imported and used in other files.
steps.hint: Add 'export default App;' at the end of the file, after the component definition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of exporting a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The export statement is placed after the component definition
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component. This makes it available for use in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're exporting the App component as the default export using 'export default App;'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component needs to be exported. Add 'export default App;' at the end of the file to make it available for import elsewhere.
